proposed_widenings.name: controllable_hazardous_item
proposed_widenings.justification: The sphere is a persistent world object with transient controller ownership, an action-based Arcana control attempt, a duration-limited control state, and a follow-up bonus-action movement command that resolves saves and damage when the object enters creature spaces. MagicItemMechanics only supports passive grants or single activated ability payloads; neither can honestly encode this stateful control loop.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you are within 60 feet of a sphere, you can take a Magic action to make a DC 25 Intelligence (Arcana) check. On a successful check, you control the sphere until the start of your next turn... While in control of the sphere, you can take a Bonus Action to cause it to move in one direction of your choice...

proposed_widenings.name: obliterate_creature_remains
proposed_widenings.justification: The sphere's damage has an extra deterministic rider when it reduces a creature to 0 HP: the creature is obliterated and leaves no physical remains, while possessions remain. Current effect atoms can deal damage, but they cannot express this corpse/remains state change.
proposed_widenings.evidence: A creature reduced to 0 Hit Points by this damage is obliterated, leaving its possessions behind but no other physical remains.

notes: No content .dhall/.json/.trace was produced. A placeholder passive or activation encoding would be misleading: it would lose the sphere-as-object state, the temporary controller lease, the failure-moves-toward-you branch, and the gated bonus-action movement loop. The portal/extradimensional interaction table is additional pressure but secondary to the structural family mismatch.
